newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's key leaders resolve row over elections.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's key leaders resolve row over elections.

text.p: Lebanon's key leaders have agreed to delay local elections for up to 12 months and extend the parliament's term by eight months in an apparent bid to resolve a dispute among themselves.

The cabinet, meeting under President Elias Hrawi on Tuesday night, also gave three important administrative jobs to a supporter of Hrawi, an associate of billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri and a backer of Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri.
The dispute started when Hariri withdrew the municipal election bill from parliament earlier this month.

Hrawi then attacked the prime minister, branding withdrawal of the bill unconstitutional and reiterating his commitment to holding the elections -- Lebanon's first local polls in 34 years -- as scheduled in June.

"It has been decided to prepare a bill that extends the mayors and municipal councils' mandates for a maximum period ending on April 30, 1998," Information Minister Bassem al-Sabaa said after the cabinet session.

That bill, and another to extend the parliament's mandate by eight months into the year 2000, will have to be approved by parliament. Newspapers predicted that parliament would approve the bills, given the agreement among the three leaders.
A political analyst said the compromise, reached after Syrian mediation, was important because it restored harmony as the country passed through a critical period in the Arab-Israeli peace process.
Berri, Hariri and Hrawi are all pro-Syrian and seldom take decisions without consulting Damascus, which has 35,000 troops in Lebanon and is its main powerbroker.

Berri, who had also advocated holding the elections on time, now gets an extra eight months at the head of the legislature. The next parliamentary election would be held in the spring of the year 2000.
Hariri and 21 ministers of the 30-member cabinet are MPs in Lebanon's 128-member parliament elected last September.

The cabinet meeting appointed a pro-Hariri engineer as director-general of Beirut port, a Berri supporter as board member of a public authority to rebuild Beirut's southern suburbs, and a Hrawi backer as director-general for the housing ministry.
